newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Assembly panel OKs $68 bln budget plan.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Assembly panel OKs $68 bln budget plan.

text.p: California Assembly's Budget Committee approved a $68 billion spending plan for fiscal year 1997-98 that would cut funding to state agencies but give raises to workers, lawmakers said Wednesday.
The Democrat-controlled Assembly committee said its budget proposal is balanced with a $534 million reserve, $46 million less than the reserve proposed by Republican Gov. Pete Wilson.
The Assembly budget calls for a three percent across-the-board cut for state agencies, but includes a five percent pay raise for state employees.
The Assembly committee's budget also contains funds to build a new University of California campus.
The budget does not include the 10 percent bank and corporation tax cut proposed by Wilson, but does include some targeted tax relief for small businesses.
The full Assembly is scheduled to consider the committee's budget proposal during Friday's session.
On Tuesday, the Senate's Budget and Fiscal Review Committee approved a $69 billion spending plan. The full Senate is scheduled to vote on its budget proposal Thursday.
The deadline for the state legislature to approve the budget is June 15. The 1997-1998 budget year begins July 1.
Once the Senate and Assembly approve their budget proposals, a conference committee would negotiate a compromise spending plan.
